title: The jet that ran out of fuel because of one unit
summary: Air Canada Flight 143 was fuelled using pounds instead of kilograms, lost both engines over Manitoba, and glided to a safe landing at Gimli thanks to a glider-pilot captain.

title: The wall cleaner that became Play-Doh
summary: Play-Doh began in the 1930s as a wallpaper cleaner, nearly died when coal heating faded, and was saved when a teacher gave it to children.

title: The girl who fell three kilometres and walked out of the jungle
summary: In 1971 seventeen-year-old Juliane Koepcke fell about three kilometres from a broken airliner, then followed a stream for ten days to reach loggers, the only survivor of 92.

title: The bear who was an official soldier in World War Two
summary: Polish soldiers adopted a bear cub in Iran, then enlisted him with a rank so he could board a ship to Italy, where he carried ammunition crates at Monte Cassino.

title: The pope who put a dead pope on trial
summary: In 897 Pope Stephen VI had his dead predecessor Formosus dug up and tried in court; it ended with Stephen jailed and a ban on trials of the dead.

title: The ghost ship that drifted the Arctic for decades
summary: The cargo steamer Baychimo was abandoned in Alaskan ice in 1931, then kept being sighted drifting empty until 1969, and has never been found.

title: The Roman Empire that was sold at an auction
summary: In 193 AD the Praetorian Guard auctioned the Roman throne to Didius Julianus, who lasted only 66 days before Septimius Severus took Rome.

title: The Indian king who adopted hundreds of Polish children
summary: In 1942, Maharaja Digvijaysinhji of Nawanagar sheltered hundreds of Polish refugee children at Balachadi, and Warsaw later named a square after him.

title: The dropped socket that nearly set off America's biggest warhead
summary: In 1980 a repairman dropped a socket in an Arkansas Titan II silo; it punctured the fuel tank, the missile exploded, and its warhead landed nearby without detonating.

title: The dirty flask that gave us safety glass
summary: In 1903 chemist Édouard Benedictus knocked a flask off a shelf and it cracked without shattering, which led to laminated safety glass.
